version.changelog: Initial release: bilingual PDF-to-markdown notes pipeline for Polito courses

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: polito-notes
Version: 1.0.0

The polito-notes skill automates the conversion of PDF lecture slides into bilingual markdown notes, requiring risky capabilities such as local file system read/write access and the execution of external shell commands (e.g., pdftotext and ls). While the behavior aligns with the stated academic purpose, the instructions in SKILL.md lack explicit input sanitization for user-provided course names and lecture titles used in file paths, which presents a potential risk for path traversal or shell injection. The skill targets a specific local directory structure (~/Documenti/github/polito/) and directs the agent to modify existing files, which is a high-privilege operation.

llm.summary: Instructions and requirements are internally consistent with a PDF→bilingual-notes pipeline; the skill is instruction-only, reads/writes user files, and does not request credentials or install code.

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose (convert lecture PDFs to bilingual markdown and place them in a course folder) matches the runtime instructions. Minor mismatch: SKILL.md suggests using a binary (pdftotext) or a Python script, but the registry metadata does not declare any required binaries or install steps — this means the skill assumes relevant tooling is already present on the host.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions explicitly tell the agent to read the provided PDF and to inspect and modify files under ~/Documenti/github/polito/ (list folders, infer lecture numbers, update existing notes files, and write new files). Reading and writing these local paths is expected for the task, but the skill will modify existing notes (rule 6: 'Update vs create'), which can overwrite or merge content — users should be aware and back up existing notes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or code files are present (instruction-only), which minimizes install risk. The only risk is that the instructions reference external tools (pdftotext or a Python script) but do not provide an installation step — the agent will rely on those tools being available on the host system.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, no credentials, and no config paths. It does not instruct the agent to call external services or transmit data outside the user's system, so requested access is proportionate to its purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not request persistent system privileges. It operates only when invoked and modifies files within the user's notes directory (its own data scope).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is an instruction-only pipeline that will read the supplied PDF and inspect/modify files under ~/Documenti/github/polito/. Before using it: 1) Ensure you have pdftotext or an equivalent PDF-to-text tool (or provide a Python extractor) on the machine; the skill does not install these. 2) Back up your notes folder — the workflow can update existing notes and may merge or overwrite content. 3) Confirm you are comfortable with the agent writing files to the target path or provide an alternative folder path. 4) The skill does not request network access or credentials, but review any PDFs for sensitive information before processing. If you want the agent to avoid modifying existing files automatically, instruct it to write outputs to a new directory or to show a preview before saving.
